title: Latency-signal probe harness — draft
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working draft of a lightweight harness we can run locally and in CI to surface small regression signals in the serving runtime that are not caught by our existing large-scale e2e suite. Focus areas: kernel selection regressions, scheduler-induced latency tails, KV cache behavior under churn, and microburst handling of prefix and streaming workloads.

Why this lives separately
- Our full e2e runs take hours and mask tiny per-token regressions.
- Existing microbench scripts are fragmented across repos and don't capture trace-driven patterns.
- We want a reproducible, low-friction probe that developers can run pre-PR and ops can run as a quick checkpoint during rollouts.

Scope and constraints
- Not a replacement for fuzz + production traces. This is an early-warning harness for subtle perf deltas (1–10% latency or p95 regressions).
- Runs should finish within 5–15 minutes on dev hardware (single GPU or small 2x GPU canary).
- Minimal dependencies: docker-compose or k8s job, python harness, a small set of trace seeds and microbench kernels.
- Output: compact JSON summary with per-scenario metrics and a human-readable regression diff.

Design overview
- Runner: python CLI (probe-run) to execute scenarios concurrently, collect metrics, and compute deltas vs baseline snapshot.
- Scenario definition: YAML files (but for this doc we keep them inline) that specify model, sequence length distribution, kv warm/cold pattern, kernel hints, and scheduler config override.
- Trace seeding: deterministic synthetic traces that can be stretched/compressed and mutated (see "trace mutator" below). We also include 3 small real traces scrubbed from prod (Q/A legal approved).
- Baseline storage: small artifact store in S3-like or local fs (sha256-named). CI jobs pin a baseline per commit window.

Key components
1) Scenario catalog (examples)
   - chat-short-prefix: many short messages, high-turn-rate, KV cache warm start. Sequence length mostly 8–64. Kernel: default. Scheduler: low-latency bias. Purpose: catch context switch overhead and kv cache miss penalties.
   - long-history-window: single long session with many tokens (2k–6k) to exercise KV chunking, KV-merge behavior, and kernel selection for long sequences. Purpose: detect kv-cache growth regressions and large-kernel fallbacks.
   - quantized-inference-branch: small model with int8 kernels; input mix contains both compressible tokens and adversarial sequences to exercise kernel paths that fail back to float kernels. Purpose: find kernel-selection mismatches that increase p95.
   - kv-churn-burst: lots of short sessions where inputs have rapidly changing prefixes (simulate many small user sessions). Sequence lengths 16–128. Purpose: expose KV eviction thrash and scheduler queue head-of-line blocking.
   - streaming-prefix-cut: mixed small/large responses with streaming enabled and frequent mid-stream cancellations. Purpose: ensure streaming and cancel paths don't produce tail latency spikes.

2) Trace mutator
   - Small python tool to take a seed trace and apply stochastic transformations: rate scaling, token-entropy injection (simulate non-English or code-heavy tokens), prefix randomization, and artificial kernel-failure markers to simulate fallback.
   - Mutator output includes a compact header describing transformations so experiments are reproducible.

3) Kernel probe harness (microbench glue)
   - We don't reimplement kernels here; harness calls into runtime's microbench API to force kernel choices (via hint or env var) and collects low-level counters: kernel_name, time_ns, cuda_kernels_launched, memcopy_time_ns, kv_cache_hits, kv_evictions.
   - When kernel selection differs from baseline, harness captures a stack trace and runtime flags to aid triage.

4) Scheduler overrides
   - Each scenario can pass scheduling knobs: batch_timeout_ms, max_batch_tokens, preemptible_priority, queue_limits.
   - Probe runs both default scheduler and an aggressive batching config to detect regressions sensitive to scheduling heuristics.

Metrics to capture (minimal set)
- p50, p90, p95, p99 latency (ms) per request type
- per-token time (ms/token) and tokens/sec
- kernel-level timings and counts
- KV cache metrics: hits, misses, evictions, avg entry lifetime
- tail events: number of requests exceeding SLA (configurable)
- sample payloads for failing requests (first n tokens)

Regression detection heuristics
- Numerical thresholds: absolute regressions > 10ms p95 or relative regressions > 10% p95 flagged. p50 regressions require higher relative threshold (20%) to avoid noisy false positives.
- Kernel-change alert: any change in dominant kernel for a scenario triggers a medium-priority alert even if overall latency change is small.
- KV churn alert: eviction rate increase > 2x or miss-rate increase > 15% flagged.
- Composite score: weighted sum of latency delta, token throughput delta, and KV churn delta. CI fails on composite score > configured threshold.

CI integration plan (short)
- New probe job: nightly and per-merge to main branch. Fast branch-level job runs only 2–3 core scenarios. Nightly runs full suite plus seed variations.
- Baseline updates: manual promoted baselines via a small PR once per release window; allow rolling baselines for canary experiments.

Quick-run examples (dev)
- run default short suite: probe-run --scenarios=chat-short-prefix,kv-churn-burst --baseline=latest
- run against specific commit baseline: probe-run --scenarios=all --baseline=git-commit-abc123
- force kernel hint: probe-run --scenario=quantized-inference-branch --kernel-hint=force-int8
- sample output: JSON with entries for each scenario and an overall verdict.

Sample output snippet (condensed)
{
  "scenario": "kv-churn-burst",
  "p95_ms": "198",
  "p95_delta_pct": "+18%",
  "kv_eviction_rate": "0.34",
  "regressions": ["p95", "kv-evictions"]
}

Triage playbook (if probe fails)
- Step 0: Verify reproducibility: rerun with random-seed=42 and record logs.
- Step 1: Check kernel-change flag. If true: attach kernel-level timings and compare with previous invocation. Look at kernel release notes/PRs.
- Step 2: If KV churn flag: reproduce with focused kv-collector: probe-run --scenario=kv-churn-burst --kv-debug=on --sample-evictions=10. Check eviction pattern and associated sequence IDs.
- Step 3: Scheduler suspicion: rerun with scheduler profile toggles (aggressive batching vs low-latency bias). If toggles flip regression direction, open ticket tagged scheduler and prioritize a root-cause session.
- Step 4: If none of above: capture full trace (preserve stack traces), collect perf counters, and escalate to perf triage channel with attached probe output and baseline diff.

Known limitations / open questions
- Small-run variance: on dev GPUs p95 can be noisy; we mitigate by repeating each scenario 3–5 times and reporting median. Is that enough? Maybe add bootstrap CI windows.
- Kernel hint surface: forcing kernels via env var is invasive; need an in-process API for safer probing. TODO: spec API with runtime team.
- Baseline drift policy: how often to refresh baseline to avoid stale false positives? Suggest per-release baseline promotion with a guardrail window.
- Real trace coverage: scrubbed traces are limited; we need more production-like seeds (work with SRE/Privacy) — ticket created JIRA:INF-923.

Implementation TODOs (near-term)
- [ ] Minimal python runner and scenario schema (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Trace mutator prototype (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Kernel microprobe integration with runtime microbench API (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] CI job and baseline snapshotter (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Small dashboard (Redwood Console) prototype to visualize probe diffs (owner: Sofia)

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Consider a fast delta-runner that only samples top-n request shapes based on recent production telemetry to reduce test surface while staying representative.
- Could integrate with Optimize to suggest which scenarios should be importance-weighted by cost/tokens.
- If we can tag scenarios with product owner and SLA, we can auto-prioritize regressions.

Appendix: short checklist for PR authors
- run `probe-run --scenarios=short-smoke` locally before pushing
- attach probe output to PR if any scenario shows >5% p95 regression
- add note in PR description if kernel or scheduler knobs changed

End of draft — feedback welcome.

[Maya]
